control.description: Upstream configure_db unchanged: the sample database is opened read-only (SQLite URI mode=ro), as LangChain's security guidance recommends.

vulnerable.description: Controlled mutation of the control: the sample database is opened with a normal writable connection. Only the creator line changes; the upstream comment saying the connection is read-only is kept in both files (comments are stripped by the scanner's features).

data_flow.source: LLM-written SQL from the LangChain SQL agent's sql_db_query tool (simulated in the harness).
data_flow.sink: SQLDatabase execution inside engine.begin(), which commits on success.

validation.summary: Temporary SQLite database and a minimal SQLDatabase stand-in that executes like langchain-community (engine.begin()). SELECT works in both versions; a model-written DELETE removes rows only in the vulnerable version.

assumptions: The app answers questions about the sample database and never needs to change it (upstream's own comment and warning say so).
A prompt-injected or mistaken model can put a destructive statement into the SQL tool input.
limitations: No live LLM or real LangChain agent is run; SQLDatabase is replaced by a stand-in that mirrors its begin()/commit behaviour.
The user-supplied database URI branch is out of scope.
streamlit and langchain imports are replaced by stubs in the harness.
